title: How many friends of friends do you have?
hook: Ten friends each, and they have ten friends each. How many new people two steps out?

knows: everyone has about the same number of friends
doesNotKnow: that friends of friends are mostly your own friends when friends know each other, so the count two steps out is a small fraction of 10 × 9

misconception: If everyone has 10 friends, about 90 people are two steps away from you.
objective: The learner can say that in the ring village only 10 people are two steps away, not 90, because most of a friend's friends are you or your own friends; 10 × 9 holds only when no two friends know each other.

claims.text: In a ring of 1,000 where each person knows the 5 nearest on each side (10 friends), 10 people are exactly 1, 2 and 3 steps away, 31 are within 3 steps counting you, and the farthest person is 100 steps away. The stage table and the reveal quote 10 at step 2, 10 at step 3 and 31 within 3.
claims.source: Node breadth-first search from person 0 on the 1,000-ring (RING_DIST in Demo.tsx, same rule as check N10 in company/domains/briefs/checks/math-ncm-wave-j-check.mjs). Builder ran N10 2026-10-22: ring {d1:10,d2:10,d3:10,within3:31,maxDist:100}. By hand: people at distance k are ±(5k−4)…±5k, 10 per step.

claims.text: If no two of anyone's friends know each other, each of your 10 friends brings 9 new people (its 10 friends minus you), giving 90 people at 2 steps and 810 at 3 (911 within 3 steps, counting you).
claims.note: Condition too weak: 'no two of anyone's friends know each other' (triangle-free) does not give 90/810; K10,10 is a counterexample. State 'no shared friends' (tree to 3 steps). See company/reviews/friends-of-friends-overlap/2026-10-22-fact-check-v2.md.

claims.text: In the village, the ringed friend (3 places to your right) knows 10 people: you, 6 of your own friends and only 3 new people.
claims.source: Friend +3 knows −2…+8 except itself: you (0); your friends −2, −1, +1, +2, +4, +5 (6); new +6, +7, +8 (3). Demo.tsx ringedLinks.

claims.text: Multiplying friends by friends (10 × 9) assumes none of your friends know each other; when friends know each other, some friends of friends are already your friends, so the count two steps out is smaller.
claims.source: Easley and Kleinberg, Networks, Crowds, and Markets (2010), ch. 20, The Small-World Phenomenon (Fig. 20.1: triadic closure slows the growth of friends-of-friends counts; section unconfirmed). Re-cited from ch. 2 after the v1 fact-check; needs a human source check (book PDFs blocked by the proxy). Holds in this stage by c1 and c2.
claims.note: E&K ch. 20 Fig. 20.1 not confirmable here: full texts blocked by the proxy; needs a human source check with the book.

recall.question: In a club everyone has 20 friends, and most of your friends know each other. Roughly how many people are friends of your friends but not your friends?
recall.why: When your friends know each other, many of their friends are already your friends, so 20 × 19 counts the same people again and again.
